title: Building Bridges: Safe Interactions with Foreign Languages through Omniglot
problem: Programming systems need to safely interoperate across multiple programming languages, but current foreign function interfaces (FFI) lack robust safety guarantees and can introduce security vulnerabilities or runtime errors at language boundaries.
motivation: Modern distributed and heterogeneous systems rely on components written in different languages, requiring safe and efficient cross-language communication to prevent exploits and ensure correctness.
method: Omniglot provides a framework for safe foreign language interactions through controlled marshalling and type-checked bindings across language boundaries. It likely enforces safety properties via runtime checks or static analysis to prevent common FFI vulnerabilities while minimizing performance overhead.
key_novelty: Safe foreign language interface abstraction that prevents common cross-language vulnerabilities while maintaining interoperability performance.
contributions: Safety guarantees and vulnerability prevention for FFI
Mechanisms for type-safe data marshalling across languages
limitations: Scope, performance characteristics, and applicability limitations not discussed in title only.
